title: How Wide Can French Spreads Get?
text:
How Wide Can French Spreads Get?

Cedric Gemehl

Gavekal Research | 1 Oct 2026

Over the last three weeks of September, the sovereign yield spread between 10-year French OATs and 10-year German bunds widened 40bp, hitting 127bp on Wednesday. That is a gap last seen in June 2012, just weeks before Mario Draghi’s “whatever it takes” speech. Inevitably, therefore, France’s current bond market stresses have evoked memories of the euro crisis, and left investors wondering: just how wide could French spreads get this time around?Before attempting to answer, it is important to point out two major differences between today and the euro crisis of the early 2010s. First, while France is the focus of present concerns, it was little more than an unfortunate bystander in the euro crisis. That episode centered on the eurozone’s peripheral economies, notably Greece, whose spread at one point exceeded 3,500bp. Through much of the euro crisis, French yields were actually falling; the widening of the French spread occurred because German yields fell faster. Today, French yields are rising outright, and France is at the frontier of eurozone spread widening.
